title: The cumulant kappa_r is platykurtic (kurtosis->3 from BELOW): a one-sided Markov-Krein with the WRONG-SIGN constraint the SOS no-go ignored
evidence: Probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C075_platykurtic_lp.py runs EXACTLY the extremal LP the connection's attack_plan specifies: largest support atom t_max of a symmetric mean-0 measure on [-sqrt(n), sqrt(n)] (the support cap is sqrt(n) because |eta_b|<=n => |X|=|eta_b|/sqrt(n)<=sqrt(n)) with m=(p-1)/n atoms, mu_2=1 (Parseval/E_1=n) AND the platykurtic inequality mu_4 <= 3-3/n (the proven in-tree value E_2=3n^2-3n => mu_4=3-3/n, verified n=8->168, n=16->720). Two facts kill the route, both exact: (1) t_ineq/t_eq = 1.0000 for EVERY proper-subgroup prize row (n=8,16,32,64 at beta=4,5; n=2^20,2^30 at beta=5): imposing mu_4<=3-3/n gives the IDENTICAL max-atom as the equality mu_4=3 the 'SOS no-go' used. The strict-below 'wrong-sign' constraint buys EXACTLY NOTHING. (2) The extremal max-atom equals the support cap exactly, t_max = sqrt(n) (t_ineq/S=1.0000 every row), which is ABOVE the prize target sqrt(2 ln m) by a factor that GROWS with prize size: 0.98x (n=16) -> 1.6x (n=64) -> 97x (n=2^20) -> 2541x (n=2^30). Diagnostic: at the extremal the 4th moment actually USED is ~1.0-1.1, far below both K=3-3/n and 3 -- the 4th-moment constraint is entirely SLACK (non-binding); the binding constraint is the support cap S=sqrt(n). The connection's premise ('the no-go rests on kurtosis-3 admitting a far atom') is false: the no-go's far atom has mass 1/m at the support edge, costing only (2/m)n^2 in 4th moment, so kurtosis-3-vs-strictly-below is a microscopic perturbation of an already-inactive constraint. Same wall as docs/kb/deltastar-407-markovkrein-and-selfimprove-walls-2026-06-13.md: any low-even-moment route (sharp or not, one-sided or two) yields sqrt(n)*poly(m), never sqrt(n*log m).
wall: W-Johnson (the moment/Markov-Krein wall: low even moments + support cap give only the trivial Cantelli sqrt(n) ceiling; the true B=sqrt(n*log m) lives in the deep far-tail/log-m extreme-value regime invisible to any fixed-order moment, the recognized BGK square-root-cancellation core).
honest_note: The platykurtic FACT (mu_4 = 3-3/n < 3, sub-Gaussian-ish via Marcinkiewicz, support |X|<=sqrt(n)) is genuinely true and is in-tree (SubgroupGaussSumFourthMoment.lean / E_2=3n^2-3n). The connection's ERROR is conjecturing this sign constraint changes the extremal bound: it does not, because the constraint is non-binding for the tiny-mass (1/m) far atom that drives the worst case. Numerics use double precision for |eta| magnitudes only via the analytic moment identities; the LP itself is exact (the extremal of a symmetric 2-moment+support problem is a single-radius 'rest' + the +-t atom pair, computed in closed form, binary-searched to 1e-12). The 6th moment (mu_6=15-45/n+40/n^2<15, also platykurtic) would add a 3rd active constraint but is likewise slack at the support-cap extremal -- the moment-count deficit Theta(log m) (KB note) is the structural reason no finite moment list closes the gap. This route should be appended to DISPROOF_LOG as the 'one-sided/platykurtic Markov-Krein' variant of the existing moment-problem no-go.
